It assumes linearity and normalization, which may fail when accounting for context such as role specialization or opponent strength. Team Strategy Networks model gameplay as a stochastic process, leveraging transition probabilities between discrete game states. This requires strong Markov assumptions, which break down during complex strategic shifts or when hidden states influence behavior. Causal inference frameworks aim to disentangle correlation from causation in performance outcomes, addressing issues like multicollinearity and confounding. These frameworks rely on identifying valid instruments or randomized experiments, failing when unmeasured heterogeneity distorts estimates.
